meta.title: Grit: Why Effort Counts Twice as Much as Talent

paragraphs.text: With those born with natural talents, it feels as if they excel without really trying. But what about those of us who don't have a natural talent? We've been told all our lives that if you work hard, you too can succeed. But with the release of Angela Duckworth's Grit, we are given a new key to success.

paragraphs.text: Duckworth says grit is the difference between success and failure. A person who has grit is more likely to succeed than a person who does not. When we think about attaining success—whether it's landing that job or learning that new skill—our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn. If you want that new job, you have to learn the job skills, then the interview skills, then the dress part—and you must be perfect at all of them. Grit is different because it tells us that perfection isn't the goal.

told.sense: 告诉、讲述、吩咐、吩咐（tell 的过去式/过去分词）

more.confusables: tell sb sth = tell sth to sb（告诉，双宾语）/ tell sb to do（叫某人做，接不定式）/ tell 与 say（say 接内容，tell 须接人）/ tell 与 speak / talk / be told to do（被动加 to）/ tell-told-told

examples: We've been told all our lives that if you work hard, you too can succeed. 从小到大总有人跟我们说：肯下功夫，你一样能成事。

transform.sense: 使改观、转变、改造、彻底改变（transform A into B；名词 transformation）
examples: Even if you haven't mastered a skill, grit tells you that you can still succeed if you can transform your passion into action. 哪怕手艺还没练到家，grit 也说：只要把喜欢的事真动手做起来，你照样能成。

trying.sense: 尝试、努力、试用（try 的现在分词）；令人难受的、费劲的

wanted.sense: 想要（want to do / want sb to do）；需要（want 的过去式/过去分词形式）

more.confusables: wanted（过去式/过去分词）/ want（原形）

way.sense: 方法、方式；路；程度（in a way）

more.confusables: we've（we have）/ we'd（we would/had）

what's.sense: what is 或 what has 的缩写

wider.sense: 更宽的、更宽阔的、更广泛的（wide 的比较级；a wider range/context 更广的范围/更宏观的背景）

without.sense: 没有、不带（后接名词或动名词）

work.sense: 工作；运转、奏效 / 工作、作品
